title: En consecuencia: expresar el resultado directo de algo

sections.content: En consecuencia (as a consequence, therefore) states the direct result of something just described -- a formal connector common in explaining economic or historical cause-and-effect chains, one step at a time. It typically opens a new sentence or clause. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Los países exportadores de petróleo acumularon enormes cantidades de dólares; en consecuencia, los bancos se encontraron con un exceso de capital.
items.english: Oil-exporting countries accumulated enormous amounts of dollars; as a consequence, banks found themselves with a surplus of capital.

items.spanish: La deuda externa se multiplicó varias veces; en consecuencia, algunos países destinaban buena parte de sus ingresos únicamente al pago de intereses.
items.english: External debt multiplied several times over; as a consequence, some countries devoted a good part of their income solely to paying interest.

items.spanish: Las tasas de interés subieron bruscamente; en consecuencia, la deuda se volvió, de la noche a la mañana, mucho más cara de pagar.
items.english: Interest rates rose sharply; as a consequence, the debt became, overnight, far more expensive to pay.

items.spanish: Varios gobiernos no pudieron cumplir con sus pagos; en consecuencia, tuvieron que negociar nuevos términos con sus acreedores.
items.english: Several governments couldn't meet their payments; as a consequence, they had to negotiate new terms with their creditors.

sections.content: En consecuencia is more formal than por eso or así que -- it fits especially well when linking a clear economic or political cause to its measurable effect, one sentence at a time.
